clue.text: Redhead wearing miniskirt gets summary dismissal

indicators.note: the miniskirt is worn around the red head, so it encloses that letter

parts.note: a short shift is a brief straight dress, a miniskirt
the head, or first letter, of the word red

explanation.surface: A red-haired woman in a miniskirt is curtly sent packing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redhead' looks like a woman with red hair; it is just the R at the head of 'red', worn inside SHORT SHIFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Short shrift is an idiom for brusque, unsympathetic treatment, a curt brush-off.

clue.text: Radio people who pretend the first shall be last?

indicators.note: a biblical phrase used literally: the opening letter of the word moves to the end

parts.note: a sham is a person who pretends to be what they are not

explanation.surface: A biblical saying is applied to broadcasters who are only pretending.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAM with its first letter S sent to the end. Radio hams are amateur radio operators.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateur radio enthusiasts are commonly called radio hams.

clue.text: Unusual combination of gunner and engineer

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, home of gunners
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: An odd pairing of an artilleryman and a sapper.
explanation.walkthrough: RA and RE are standard abbreviations for two British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare is seldom found, uncommon.

clue.text: Caused an obstruction, but unusally mystified if dropped

indicators.note: read as unusually (the clue's own spelling), meaning the letters are arranged in an odd new order

parts.note: the word supplies letters as printed
the word supplies the letters taken out

explanation.surface: Someone is puzzled about why something got blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I and F ('if dropped') from MYSTIFIED and rearrange the rest ('unusally', a misspelling of unusually in the clue).
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie is to block or thwart, so stymied means hindered someone's progress.

clue.text: Horse that dashed around the ring

indicators.note: the running word goes around the ring shape, enclosing it

parts.note: dashed means ran quickly
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A horse galloped round the circus ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse whose coat is flecked with white hairs.

clue.text: Footballers are on time before matches with heavyweights

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come in front of the word for matches

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, governing English football
cup ties are football matches

explanation.surface: A soccer team on the clock prepares to face hefty opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are on' is just link wording joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavyweights here means overweight people, informally called fatties.

clue.text: Amount of money initially paid for oil deposit

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word paid is taken

explanation.surface: A payment is made upfront for an oil reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A sump is the reservoir at the bottom of an engine where oil collects.

clue.text: Tactics needed for a job serving in the restaurant?

definitions.text: a job serving in the restaurant?

explanation.surface: A waiter's job requires its own strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading treats 'waiting' as waiting at tables and 'game' as one's line of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Biding one's time for an advantage is a strategy, and table service is a waiter's line of work.

clue.text: Brass player writing article on old boat

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the article is placed after the boat

parts.note: a tub is a slow, clumsy old boat
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A trombonist writes a piece about an ancient vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: This large low-pitched instrument belongs to the brass section, so it plays the brass part.

clue.text: Sting gasps about youth leader being a know-all

indicators.note: the two words surround the youth leader, holding it between them

parts.note: to smart is to sting
pants means gasps for breath

indicators.note: the leading, first letter of the word youth

explanation.surface: A wasp's sting leaves a young leader gasping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sting' reads as a verb or the singer, but it is a synonym that pairs with 'gasps' to surround the youth's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A smarty-pants is a show-off who thinks they know everything.

clue.text: Father found in street argument

indicators.note: the father is located inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad is spotted in the middle of a row out in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a short petty quarrel.

clue.text: Hold a blonde tight, and there you are!

indicators.note: tight here means drunk, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to hug a fair-haired person closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' seems to describe the embrace but signals rearranging HOLD A BLONDE.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic exclamation presents something surprising, much like voila.

clue.text: Tidy odds on game with Carlisle, on the surface

parts.note: SP is starting price, the betting odds
RU is rugby union

indicators.note: only the outside letters of Carlisle, its exterior, are used

explanation.surface: A neat bet is placed on a match involving Carlisle United.
explanation.walkthrough: Carlisle is an English town with a football club, which shapes the betting picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To spruce or spruce up is to make neat and smart.

clue.text: Struck an attitude against work?

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
posed means struck an attitude

explanation.surface: Someone strikes a pose in protest at having to work.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits in the middle of the clue; OP comes first in the answer though 'work' is last.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed means being against something.

clue.text: Interior design firm registered following disheartening debate

indicators.note: the firm and registered letters come after the debate remnant
removing the heart of debate leaves only its first and last letters

parts.note: CO is company, a firm
R is short for registered, as in a trademark

explanation.surface: A design company signs up after a dispiriting discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the style of furnishing and decoration inside a room.

clue.text: Rent day precedes personal disappointment

indicators.note: the rent and day pieces come before the word for personal

parts.note: to let is to rent out
own means belonging to oneself, personal

explanation.surface: Rent day comes round just before a private setback.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-down is a disappointing anticlimax.

clue.text: Deposit required for temporary accommodation

explanation.surface: A deposit must be paid for a short-term place to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge is to deposit something; a lodge is also a cabin or gatehouse used for short stays.

clue.text: Screaming the first two are dropped is revealing

indicators.note: the opening two letters of the word for screaming are left off

parts.note: shouting means screaming

explanation.surface: Someone yells while explaining what has been exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Outing someone is exposing their secret, such as sexuality, to the public.

clue.text: Presentations are made mostly therein

indicators.note: the letters lie in the words just named, made mostly

explanation.surface: Most talks are produced in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: Demos are demonstrations showing a product or skill.

clue.text: A refusal before America shows common sense

indicators.note: the refusal comes in front of America

parts.note: no is a refusal
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Saying no to America is presented as wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is British slang for practical intelligence and shrewdness.

clue.text: Animal bearing a label

parts.note: S is south, a compass bearing
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A creature wears an identification tag.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is a male deer.

clue.text: Dissolute man, around middle-age, with make-up

indicators.note: the dissolute man surrounds the middle letter

parts.note: a roue is a debauched man
G is the middle letter of age

explanation.surface: An ageing rake wears cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle-age' reads as midlife but gives the centre letter of 'age'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouge is red cosmetic powder for the cheeks.

clue.text: Rising nervous reaction in true to life performance

indicators.note: the reversed twitch goes inside the word for true to life

parts.note: real means true to life

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A nervous twitch shows during a realistic stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' works because this is a down entry: the twitch is read from the bottom up before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a concert or performance, often by a soloist.

clue.text: Disease that's terminal to mice, perhaps

parts.note: an end is a terminal point

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word mice could be put another way, rearranged

explanation.surface: A disease that proves fatal to mice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminal' looks like fatal but gives END; EMIC is MICE rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Endemic describes a disease regularly found in a region; here used for the disease itself.

clue.text: How might one mix it with a student in a booze-up?

indicators.note: the student goes inside the booze-up

parts.note: a bender is a drinking spree
L is a learner, a student

explanation.surface: A question about mingling with a student at a drinking party.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner (from British learner-driver plates) is the student.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen appliance one might use to mix ingredients.

clue.text: Poison even changes structure with negative mass

indicators.note: the word even is rebuilt in a different order

parts.note: no is a negative
M is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A poison alters its makeup when combined with negative mass.
explanation.definitionFit: To envenom is to make poisonous or to inject venom.

clue.text: Tried to get rid of a number of cattle

indicators.note: the letter given by a is removed from the word for tried

parts.note: a case tried in court is heard

explanation.surface: Someone attempted to dispose of some cows.
explanation.walkthrough: HEARD, as a court hears or tries a case, loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a group of cattle.

clue.text: Sweetheart's after free travel

indicators.note: the heart letter comes after the word for free

parts.note: to rid is to free
E is the heart, the middle letter, of sweet

explanation.surface: A lover is after a free trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to travel on a horse or vehicle.

clue.text: Personal problem that's new in service

indicators.note: the new letter goes inside the service

parts.note: an ace is a winning tennis serve

explanation.surface: A private worry arises in military service.
explanation.definitionFit: This skin condition is a common and embarrassing personal affliction.

clue.text: Humour is about right for a legal document

indicators.note: the humour word goes around the letter for right

parts.note: wit is humour

explanation.surface: Humour is the right touch for a legal paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal written court order.

clue.text: Note from the doctor accepting the compiler is up

indicators.note: in a down entry, being up puts the compiler above the doctor

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor's note admits the puzzle setter is out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' is only link wording; in a down entry 'is up' means the setter's word sits above the doctor's.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is a short written message or reminder.

clue.text: Share trading area for farm animals?

explanation.surface: A place where shares are traded seems fit for livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Shares are bought and sold on a stock exchange; a livestock sale is literally a market for stock.

clue.text: Cover round pool!

parts.note: a lid is a cover
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A covering is put around a swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool.

clue.text: Argument over an article to be edited

indicators.note: editing changes text around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over a piece due for editing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link word; the fodder includes 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: An altercation is a noisy quarrel.
